hypothesis: The deterministic one-repair-per-update lazy EDCS variant preserves P1/P2 and a 2/3 finite matching-ratio endpoint on the declared small bipartite domain.

method.domain: all labeled bipartite masks k=1,2,3; all K3,3 deletion prefixes lengths 1..6; one greedy mixed depth-6 trajectory

falsification_gate.rule: A state with used-edge degree sum > beta falsifies the frozen lazy-variant invariant.

observed_result_or_blocker: The frozen one-flip lazy rule inserts (1,0) to repair a P2 deficiency but leaves used edge (0,0) at degree sum 5>4. The exact matching ratio remains 1.0, so this is an invariant-maintenance failure rather than a matching-ratio failure.
uncertainty: The result is finite and applies only to the exact deterministic variant, beta values and update semantics frozen here.
The counterexample does not refute Bernstein-Stein EDCS existence, matching theorems or their alternating-path/orientation/bucket maintenance algorithm.
The source-level novelty audit found no claim that this finite variant counterexample is a new theorem or general dynamic-matching result.
limitations: No asymptotic or production update-time conclusion.
The matching-ratio endpoint was not falsified in the minimal witness.
